answer: An inlet of cheap seats opens when the only bond is the answer box. Paste-miners flood it because a vignette costs seconds and a grader minute costs the panel real inventory. The karst under that flood is hollow identity: clones share one prompt and diverge only in seed-word paint. Quartz here is a hashed agent session — omit the human turn and the crystal cracks; split the desk and two hashes cannot occupy one seat. Jury time stays scarce. Cheap inlets silt up.
